title: Plantation bells and the field work day
summary: Describes the plantation bell schedule, the working day, and his father as foreman.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, I think of it, after we talked to Sonny Henry, the next day we saw him, he said, Oh, I forgot to tell you about the big bell or something down at Magnolia.
Or did he go, used to go to work? I don't know what it was, he didn't tell us.
He said he forgot to tell us on the big plantation bell.
Oh yeah, he got a big bell that sets up on like a tower. And they would ring one about, in the summertime, they'd ring a bell about, about 4 or 4.15 in the morning.
In the morning, is that right?

Yeah, in the morning, it was daylight. It's now daylight, it'd be daylight around, 4.30 is putting that daylight. Then they'd ring the others around, but, but, about 15 minutes apart anyhow, they'd ring, they used to call it the first bell and the second bell. And A and A gets up there and go ahead and go around the stable and get the mule and then get on out there. Sometime when you get out of there and be going out there, you'll be near to your work, a mile, sometime a half a mile, the sun don't just be peeping up sometime. But the gladdest sun in the morning is day, but the sun don't be up. You can see the rays of it coming up. And you start out there and then around about 7 o'clock or 7.30, a boy would bring you breakfast. A fellow with a water boy, he's bringing breakfast out there. And you'd have it half an hour, sit down, eat breakfast, and you'd get up and go again. Maybe 11 o'clock when the sun hot, you knock off around about 11 o'clock, you know. You go home, you come out about 1 or 1.30, you come back. And then you'd have to tell it about 6.30.
Did they ring a bell at noon all the time for that too?

They had a bell at noon, yeah. All the time. You didn't need to be right up on the pump with the bell, you know. See, when the bell rings, you'll be home. That didn't mean for you to come to work. It didn't mean for you to go, be on the job at the bell, you know. You leave home. Well, I used to like my daddy. He was a foreman, you know. And when I was young, younger all my brothers' wife was giving their money to my daddy. So they built a house, place, and thing just about a mile and a half from there. And my brother went and lived over there. One of the oldest brothers, he made chalk and fish, you see, and trap.
